title: Interactive Span Focus Transitions — Journal + Wireframes
body:
Purpose / quick context:
This doc captures a week+ of whiteboarding and lightweight wireframes around how span focus should behave inside the trace waterfall view. Goal: reduce cognitive load when drilling into deep traces, keep timeline context, and make keyboard-first workflows reliable for SREs and engineers investigating tail latency.

Problem statement:
- Current behaviour (prototype v2): clicking a span opens a right-side detail pane and highlights the span, but the waterfall viewport often scrolls unexpectedly, losing local context; keyboard nav is inconsistent (up/down sometimes jumps to unrelated spans).
- Consequences: slow investigation cycles, user frustration when jumping between nearby spans, hard to compare sibling spans across long traces.

Hypotheses we want to validate:
1) If focus transitions preserve viewport anchor (the focused span stays vertically in the same pixel location), engineers can compare before/after values faster.
2) Animating focus transitions (200ms ease-out) provides better mental continuity than instant jumps but must be subtle to not hide timing details.
3) Keyboard pivots (focus left/right/up/down) should map to semantic relationships (parent/sibling/first-child/next-span) rather than naive DOM order.

Design constraints and principles:
- Non-destructive: opening details or toggling expanders should not reorder spans.
- Preserve timeline scale: zoom level and X-axis remain stable when focusing.
- Accessibility: all focus transitions must be invokable by keyboard and have ARIA announcements (e.g., "Focused span: service=db, duration 124ms").
- Performance: no extra server calls when moving focus within the same trace; only prefetch details for immediate neighbors.

Wireframe notes (text sketches):
1) Compact focus overlay (default)
   - Visual: thin 1px bright outline + soft 8px glow on focused span row.
   - Behavior: detail preview flies out as ephemeral overlay above the waterfall (not the full right panel). Overlay shows top 3 fields (service, op, duration) and two quick-actions (re-run, open full pane).
   - Use-case: quick skim through spans without losing vertical pattern.

2) Sticky anchor mode (toggleable)
   - Visual: the focused span occupies a pinned slot (approx center of viewport) when toggled on; other spans scroll around it.
   - Behavior: toggled by pressing "a" or clicking pin icon. Anchor remembers last X-axis viewport position to avoid timeline jumps.
   - Use-case: longer comparisons — user pins a span, then navigates siblings to compare durations.

3) Full detail pane (existing) improvements
   - When opening full pane, keep focused span in viewport and slide pane from right with 220ms animation; do not auto-scroll the waterfall except to ensure the focused span is visible (minimally).

Interaction flows (keyboard + mouse):
- Mouse: hover previews after 350ms, click focuses. CTRL+click opens full pane in split mode. Right-click menu includes "Pin span", "Copy duration", "Open parent in new view".
- Keyboard (proposed mapping):
  - ArrowUp / ArrowDown: move focus to previous/next visible span in the current collapsed/expanded state (not strictly DOM order — prefer chronological/topological).
  - ArrowLeft: go to parent span (if exists); if none, move to previous sibling's parent.
  - ArrowRight: go to first child span (if collapsed, expand then focus child).
  - P: toggle pin/anchor mode.
  - Enter: open full detail pane.
  - Shift+Enter: open full detail pane and jump to request/response logs pane.

Micro-interaction notes:
- Animations: 160–220ms duration; use cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) easing. Avoid opacity changes that hide timing bars.
- Highlighting: use saturated accent for outline and low-opacity accent fill for a ~12px buffer to draw attention without obscuring text.
- Focus ring: must be 3px for keyboard focus (WCAG).

Data model and perf considerations (engineering notes):
- Prefetch pattern: when a span gets focus, enqueue prefetch for siblings +/-3 and parent/first-child. Tag this as low priority network requests cached for 30s.
- Minimal payload for preview overlay: { service, op, start_ts, end_ts, tags[important], error_flag } (we only store as columnar values — doc will reference schema).
- Event telemetry: capture focus_event with attributes: from_span_id, to_span_id, nav_method (mouse/keyboard), pin_state. Will help measure hypothesis 1/2.

Open questions / tradeoffs (unresolved):
- Should anchor mode be global per-trace or per-user session? (Proposal: per-trace until refresh.)
- How to handle very small viewports (mobile / narrow consoles): disable sticky anchor and use top-floating preview only?
- When many spans have identical start_ts (parallel children), how to choose ArrowDown order? (Prefer visual left-to-right ordering rather than ID order.)

Acceptance criteria (for a grooming ticket):
- Focus transitions keep focused span at same vertical pixel when possible (unit tests + manual checks across traces with depth 1–20).
- Keyboard mappings work consistently in collapsed and expanded states.
- Prefetch for 3 neighbors implemented and cached for 30s.
- Telemetry events emitted for focus changes.

Backlog items (rough JIRA-style list)
- INF-1412: Implement anchor toggle + pin UX (gate behind feature flag).
- INF-1413: Keyboard nav mapping and behavior tests; include unit tests for collapsed tree state.
- INF-1414: Preview overlay component + minimal backend endpoint for preview payload.
- INF-1415: Animation polish + accessibility audits (VPAT notes).
- INF-1416: Telemetry schema for focus_event.

Design experiments (A/B ideas):
- Variant A: transient overlay on hover (350ms), no animation on focus change.
- Variant B: persistent preview pane docked left of the waterfall (sacrifices width).
- Metrics to compare: mean investigation time per trace, number of full pane opens, keyboard-first adoption rate.

Notes from recent usability run (internal session 2024-12-12):
- Observers: 6 infra engineers, tasks: find slowest child span and compare to sibling.
- Findings: participants liked pinned center but wanted an affordance to "freeze" X-axis zoom. Several accidentally lost context when the panel opened because the UI auto-scrolled too far.
- Action: disable auto-zoom on panel open; prefer minimal scroll-to-visible.

Next steps / who does what:
- Maya: draft Figma frames for compact overlay + pinned center (due 2024-11-20).
- Diego: backend preview endpoint sketch + estimated cost (2024-11-22).
- Priya: accessibility checklist + initial screen-reader copy (2024-11-18).
- Owen: prototype keyboard nav and telemetry (spike, 1 week).

Loose sketches (textual):
[waterfall viewport]
|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| span row 1                                                   |
| span row 2   <-- focused (outlined + glow)  [preview overlay] |
| span row 3                                                   |
| ...                                                          |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|

Pinned anchor mock: (center pinned)
|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| span row -3                                                  |
| span row -2                                                  |
| span row -1                                                  |
| [ PINNED -> focused span ]                                   |
| span row +1                                                  |
| span row +2                                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as the canonical discussion thread for the next grooming session; avoid merging with other trace-wireframe docs to preserve exploratory rationale.

Unresolved UX copy ideas:
- Pin button tooltip: "Pin focus — keep this span fixed while navigating"
- Preview CTA: "Open pane" vs "Inspect" (leaning to Inspect).

End.
